Campaign notes:
- Angles tested: mostly B (quality/craftsmanship); D (customer testimonial) used on Days 6–7. No A (price cut) or C (limited urgency) tested.
- Results are delayed and aggregated, not attributable to individual days or angles:
  - Day 5 report: 3 of last 5 pushes landed.
  - Day 10 report: 2 of last 5 pushes landed.
- Quality messaging has not demonstrated a clear advantage; performance appears variable. Avoid treating the two aggregate reports as proof of causation.
- Refreshed design/banner art appeared repeatedly and can support craftsmanship/presentation messaging, but its impact is unmeasured.
- Deliverability was generally stable: no complaints on most days. Two unsubscribes arrived via support on Day 9 and were processed.
- Continue monitoring unsubscribes and deliverability. To learn which message works, rotate angles deliberately (including A/C or another D test) and record results by day whenever possible.
- Prefer credible, non-pressuring claims; do not infer that evergreen quality messaging is safer or more effective without breakdown data.

Campaign notes:
- Angles used through Day 20: B (quality/craftsmanship), D (customer testimonial), A (price cut), and C (limited urgency). Recent sequence: D (Days 11, 13, 17, 19), A (Days 12, 15, 16, 18), C (Day 14), and C (Day 20).
- Outcomes remain delayed and aggregated, not attributable to individual days or angles:
  - Day 5: 3 of last 5 pushes landed.
  - Day 10: 2 of last 5 landed.
  - Day 15: 2 of last 5 landed, following several A sends.
  - Day 20: 4 of last 5 landed, following a C send.
- These reports do not establish that A or C caused the changes; avoid claiming any angle is superior without per-send breakdowns.
- Quality messaging still has no demonstrated advantage. D has now had multiple tests, including after refreshed banner art on Day 13, but its impact is unmeasured.
- Deliverability has remained stable: no new complaints reported during Days 11–20. Two support-submitted unsubscribes from Day 9 were processed; continue monitoring.
- Use deliberate rotation and record per-day opens/conversions when possible. Keep claims credible and non-pressuring.
- Do not imply false scarcity. If using C, urgency must be genuine, specific, and transparent. A must clearly state the actual price change and terms.
- Continue testing A, C, and D against B, ideally with consistent audiences and enough volume for comparable results.

Campaign notes:
- Through Day 20, angles used were B (quality/craftsmanship), D (customer testimonial), A (price cut), and C (limited urgency). Recent pre-Day-21 sequence: D on Days 11, 13, 17, 19; A on Days 12, 15, 16, 18; C on Days 14 and 20.
- Days 21–30 used B exclusively. Banner art was refreshed around Days 24, 28, and 30; this does not isolate the effect of either B or the design changes.
- Aggregate reports remain delayed and un attributable to individual sends:
  - Day 20: 4 of last 5 landed, after C.
  - Day 25: 1 of last 5 landed, after repeated B.
  - Day 30: 1 of last 5 landed, after repeated B.
  No per-day opens or conversion breakdowns were available, so do not infer that B or refreshed art caused the decline.
- Earlier results likewise do not establish that A, C, D, or B is superior. Quality messaging has now had an extended B run, but its impact remains unmeasured.
- List growth occurred intermittently (Days 21, 23, 25, and 29), potentially affecting aggregate comparisons. Record audience size and composition.
- Two support-submitted unsubscribes were reported and processed on Day 27; continue monitoring deliverability and complaints.
- Resume deliberate rotation rather than continuing B exclusively. Test A, C, and D against B with consistent audiences, adequate volume, and per-send opens/conversions.
- Keep claims credible and non-pressuring. C requires genuine, specific, transparent urgency; A must state the actual price change and terms. Do not imply false scarcity.

Campaign notes:
- Through Day 20, angles used were B (quality/craftsmanship), D (customer testimonial), A (price cut), and C (limited urgency). Days 21–30 used B exclusively; Days 31–40 used D on Days 31 and 33–40, with A on Day 32. This creates prolonged B and D runs, not clean comparisons.
- Banner art was refreshed around Days 24, 28, and 30, so design effects remain confounded with angle and timing.
- Aggregate reports are delayed and not attributable to individual sends:
  - Day 20: 4 of last 5 landed, after C.
  - Day 25 and Day 30: 1 of last 5 each, after repeated B.
  - Day 35: 2 of last 5, during repeated D.
  - Day 40: 0 of last 5, after continued D.
  Do not infer that B, D, or refreshed art caused declines; no per-day opens, conversions, or delivery breakdowns are available.
- No angle is proven superior. Resume deliberate rotation and avoid extended single-angle runs. Test A, B, C, and D with consistent audiences, adequate volume, fixed send timing, and per-send opens, conversions, unsubscribes, complaints, and delivery.
- List growth occurred repeatedly (Days 21, 23, 25, 29, and several Days 32–37). Record audience size and composition for every send; growth may distort aggregate comparisons.
- Support-reported unsubscribes were processed on Day 27 and Day 40; no deliverability complaints were reported on Days 38–39. Continue monitoring unsubscribes, complaints, and delivery.
- Keep claims credible and non-pressuring. C requires genuine, specific, transparent urgency; A must state actual price changes and terms. Never imply false scarcity.

Campaign notes:
- Through Day 50, no angle is proven superior. Earlier runs of B and D were prolonged and confounded; Days 41–50 used A on 41–42, 44, 46–48 and C on 43, 45, 49–50. Avoid new extended A/C runs; resume deliberate rotation across A, B, C, and D.
- Aggregate reports remain delayed and not attributable to individual sends. Day 45 and Day 50 each reported 2 of the last 5 pushes landed, but these results cannot be assigned to C or any specific send. Do not infer angle effects without per-send data.
- Banner art refreshed around Days 24, 28, 30, 41, and 47. Design effects remain confounded with angle and timing; compare creative only with controlled tests.
- List growth occurred repeatedly through Day 37 and again on Day 48. Record audience size, source, and composition for every send; new signups may distort comparisons.
- Day 46 had no reported deliverability complaints. Continue tracking unsubscribes, complaints, delivery, opens, conversions, and bounces per send. Support-reported unsubscribes were processed on Days 27 and 40.
- Maintain consistent audiences, fixed 10am timing, adequate volume, and randomized/structured angle rotation. Capture per-send metrics and audience composition separately so results can be compared.
- Legal signed off on all four angles during Days 43, 44, and 49. Keep claims credible and non-pressuring: C needs genuine, specific, transparent urgency; A must state actual price changes and terms. Never imply false scarcity.

Campaign notes:
- No angle is proven superior through Day 60. Days 51–60 used B (51, 53, 55, 57) and D (52, 54, 56, 58–60); D is now overrepresented, so resume deliberate rotation across A, B, C, and D rather than extending B/D runs.
- Aggregate reports remain delayed and cannot be attributed to individual sends. Day 55 reported 2 of the last 5 pushes landed; Day 60 reported 1 of the last 5. Do not infer angle performance from either report.
- Banner art was refreshed around Days 24, 28, 30, 41, 47, 57, and 60. Creative, angle, timing, and audience changes remain confounded; test creative only with controlled comparisons.
- The list grew again on Day 54. Record audience size, acquisition source, and composition for every send; new signups may distort comparisons.
- No deliverability complaints were reported on Days 53, 58, or 59. Continue tracking delivery, opens, conversions, unsubscribes, complaints, and bounces per send. Support-reported unsubscribes were processed on Days 27 and 40.
- Keep the 10am window, consistent audiences and volume where feasible, and randomized/structured angle rotation. Capture per-send metrics and audience composition separately; aggregate reports are insufficient.
- Legal has signed off on all four angles through Day 55. Keep claims credible and non-pressuring: C requires genuine, specific, transparent urgency; A must state actual price changes and terms. Never imply false scarcity.
